newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lion to inject S$140 mln in rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Lion to inject S$140 mln in rescue plan.

text.p: Malaysian conglomerate Lion Group will pump Singapore $140 million of assets into Lion Teck Chiang (LTC) in a rescue of Malaysian Feedmills Ltd (MFL), LTC officials said on Thursday.
LTC is the new property and steel company formed in place of MFL after Lion's rescue of the loss-making MFL earlier this year.
MFL shareholders had approved Lion's rescue plan of the former producer of animal feed and agricultural products, LTC officials told a news conference.
LTC is expected to be listed on the Singapore stock exchange by the second quarter of 1997 in place of MFL, which was suspended in June 1988.
Lion has a controlling stake of 71.7 percent in LTC. Bidara Holdings Sdn Bhd, which had 24 percent stake in MFL, will hold a six percent stake in LTC.

Teng Chai Hai, LTC's senior accountant, said Lion would inject into LTC its S$3.3 million Malaysian property development company Che Kiang Realty Sdn Bhd, its S$15 million steel company Angkasa Building Materials Pte Ltd (ABM) based in Singapore and S$73 million Singapore property firm Teck Chiang Realty Pte Ltd.
The injection includes the Malaysian land banks that Che Kiang will acquire from the Lion Group. These are valued at 65.89 million ringgit.
The restructured LTC is expected to maintain the combined growth in turnover and profits of the companies injected, LTC director Lionel Cheng said.
The three companies together recorded pretax profits of S$15.7 million on a turnover of S$115.7 million in 1995.
Cheng said land development would be the main driver of the group's future earnings. Property activities contributed 48 percent to the three companies' pre-tax earnings in 1995.
"In Malaysia, we have over 1,500 acres of land for potential development. In the next few years, income will be generated from this development," Cheng said.
He said the group would look to increase its land bank to support property development activities.
